title: Bidadi Twin-Betta Loop
tagline: Bidadi → Byramangala backwaters → Narasimhaswamy Betta (fort-hill trek) → Kanakapura → Gavi Ranganatha Betta (cave temple, mud track to the top) → Kanva reservoir → Ramanagara → Manchanabele backwaters → Bidadi. ~140 km of village roads, two hill temples, two dirt sections.
summary: A one-day loop out of Bidadi that strings together two little-visited hill temples south of Bangalore — Shri Narasimhaswamy Betta, a fort hill above Vadedoddi with stone steps and ruined ramparts, and Gavi Ranganatha (Gaviranga) Betta near Singarajapura, where the shrine sits in a cave behind a pond and a mud track climbs the hill. Between them the route deliberately stays off the Mysore highway: reservoir bund roads at Byramangala and Kanva, the granite-boulder country around Ramanagara, and a finish through the Manchanabele backwaters where the tarmac gives out into dirt. Short enough to start at 6 AM and be home for dinner, with about two hours of walking.

segments.note: Leave the highway immediately. Narrow road along the Byramangala reservoir bund — pelicans and painted storks in winter, best at first light.

segments.road: Byramangala → Kanchugaranahalli → village roads to Vadedoddi
segments.note: Single-lane village roads through ragi fields and eucalyptus. Navigate by map to 'Shri Narasimhaswamy Betta'; the last km is a concrete road behind an arch, often locked — park outside and walk.
Back to a proper road. Kanakapura is the fuel and lunch stop — the only real town on the loop.

segments.road: Kanakapura – Channapatna road, turn for Haniyuru / Singarajapura
segments.note: Rolling farmland with granite outcrops. Mud road up the hill to the temple; a stone-step trail if you'd rather walk it.
Channapatna (toy town) is the only busy bit. Turn off for Kanva — quiet bund road along the reservoir with hills all round.
Into the boulder country that Sholay was shot in. Ramadevara Betta is a short detour if daylight allows (closes 5:30 PM).
Broken village road, then the dam. Dirt tracks around the backwaters — the loop's proper off-road section.
Quiet run back to Bidadi through farmland, past the Big Banyan Tree turn-off.

highlights: Shri Narasimhaswamy Betta — an hour's climb up ancient stone steps past overgrown fort walls to a small temple and pool on top; almost nobody but villagers goes.
Gavi Ranganatha Betta — Rishyashringa's cave shrine behind a pond, Bhairaveshwara temple alongside, and a 360° view over Mari Betta, SRS hills and the lake below.
Byramangala and Kanva reservoirs — two bund roads that most riders skip, both empty at dawn.
Ramanagara's granite boulders on the Kanva road — Sholay country without the Sholay traffic.
Manchanabele backwaters at sunset — dirt tracks down to the water with Savandurga on the skyline.

offroad.summary: Mostly single-lane village tarmac with two genuine dirt sections: the mud track up Gavi Ranganatha Betta and the backwater trails at Manchanabele. Both are fine on an ADV or scrambler in the dry; on a road bike walk the hill and stop at the dam.
notes: Gavi Ranganatha mud road: loose red soil and rock steps; rideable in dry months, slick as soap after rain. Low tyre pressures help.
Manchanabele backwater tracks: soft sand near the water's edge, ruts from 4x4s. Turn around before the ground goes dark and wet — bikes sink.
Narasimhaswamy Betta: no riding above the arch. The trek is 30–60 min up with loose soil on the descent — proper shoes, not riding boots.
Village roads near Vadedoddi: unmarked speed breakers, cattle, and sudden gravel patches where the surface has been dug up.
Carry a tyre-plug kit; there is nothing between Kanakapura and Ramanagara.

timings: Gavi Ranganatha cave shrine is opened only on Saturdays and festival days — ride it on a Saturday if you want to go inside; the hill and outer temple are open daily (roughly till 6 PM).
Narasimhaswamy Betta temple opens around 8 AM; the gate road may be locked — park outside and walk.
Ramadevara Betta closes at 5:30 PM. Manchanabele dam area is best left before dark; no lighting.
Fuel: Bidadi at the start, Kanakapura mid-loop, Ramanagara near the end. Locals near Narasimhaswamy Betta sell bottled petrol in a pinch.
No permits. Both hill temples are free; small parking fee at Gavi Ranganatha.
cautions: Gavi Ranganatha's hill is surrounded by forest — bears visit the artificial pond. Don't linger after dusk, don't leave food out.
The Narasimhaswamy Betta pool is polluted by offerings; carry your own water for the trek.
Monsoon (Jun–Aug) makes both dirt sections unrideable and the stone steps slippery; the reservoirs are prettiest right after, in Sep–Oct.
Google Maps will try to put you back on the Mysore highway between Channapatna and Bidadi — ignore it and follow the Kanva/Ramanagara/Manchanabele legs.
